name: ADUM4160BRWZ-RL
title: 5 kV USB isolator for full and low speed
summary: A galvanic isolator for the D+ and D- lines of an upstream-facing USB port, built on transformer-coupled iCoupler channels. It watches both sides for activity, works out the direction of each packet and turns its output buffers on and off to suit, so the USB stream passes through with a delay close to one hub plus cable. Speed (1.5 Mbps low speed or 12 Mbps full speed) is fixed by two strap pins; the upstream pull-up and the downstream pull-downs are inside. Each side runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V bus power through an internal 3.3 V regulator, or straight from 3.3 V. The upstream side is short-circuit protected. Wide-body SOIC-16, 5000 V rms for one minute (UL 1577), in a standard and an increased-creepage version.

pins.name: VBUS1
pins.function: Side 1 supply input. Tie to the USB bus (4.5 V to 5.5 V), or, on a 3.3 V supply, tie to VDD1 and the 3.3 V rail. Needs a bypass capacitor to GND1.

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Side 1 ground. Joined inside to pin 8; connect both to GND1.

pins.name: VDD1
pins.function: Side 1 3.3 V rail. With bus power it is the regulator output: bypass it to GND1 and pull PDEN and SPU up from it. With a 3.3 V supply, tie it to VBUS1 and the supply; bypass to GND1.

pins.name: PDEN
pins.function: Pull-down enable, sampled as the part leaves reset. Tie to VDD1 for normal use. Held at GND1 while leaving reset, it disconnects the downstream pull-down resistors so buffer impedance can be measured.

pins.name: SPU
pins.function: Upstream speed select, active high. High selects the full speed edge rate, timing and J/K convention; low selects the low speed set. Strap to VDD1 or GND1; must equal SPD (pin 13).

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Side 1 ground. Joined inside to pin 2; connect both to GND1.

pins.name: GND2
pins.function: Side 2 ground. Joined inside to pin 15; connect both to GND2.

pins.name: PIN
pins.function: Upstream pull-up enable: switches power to the pull-up on the upstream port. Tie to VDD2 to attach at power-up, or drive from a control line to delay enumeration.

pins.name: SPD
pins.function: Downstream speed select, active high. High selects the full speed edge rate, timing and J/K convention; low selects the low speed set. Strap to VDD2 or GND2; must equal SPU (pin 5).

pins.name: VDD2
pins.function: Side 2 3.3 V rail. With bus power it is the regulator output: bypass it to GND2; pull-ups such as SPD may be taken from it. With a 3.3 V supply, tie it to VBUS2 and the supply; bypass to GND2.

pins.name: GND2
pins.function: Side 2 ground. Joined inside to pin 9; connect both to GND2.

pins.name: VBUS2
pins.function: Side 2 supply input. Tie to a 4.5 V to 5.5 V bus, or, on a 3.3 V supply, tie to VDD2 and the 3.3 V rail. Needs a bypass capacitor to GND2.

circuits.title: Typical application: isolated USB peripheral
circuits.description: The isolator sits between the host cable and a peripheral's microcontroller. Side 1 takes VBUS and ground from the USB host and carries the upstream data lines; side 2 runs from the peripheral's own 3.3 V supply, on VBUS2 and VDD2 together, with its data lines on the microcontroller's USB pins. A microcontroller output drives PIN, so the peripheral decides when the upstream pull-up appears and enumeration starts. The two grounds stay separate.
notes: Misprint: the side 1 data lines read DD+ and DD-; they are UD+ and UD-.
Besides the parts shown, the part needs only external series resistors and bypass capacitors to operate.

circuits.title: Recommended printed circuit board layout: bus-powered side 1, 3.3 V side 2
circuits.description: Side 1 is fed 5.0 V from the USB bus on VBUS1, and its regulator puts out 3.3 V on VDD1. Side 2 is fed 3.3 V on both VBUS2 and VDD2, which bypasses its regulator. Each supply pin has a 0.1 µF low-ESR capacitor to its own ground, and each data line has a 24 Ω ±1% series resistor for full speed. PDEN is tied to VDD1 for normal operation. SPU, SPD and PIN are brought out to be strapped: SPU and SPD to the same speed, PIN high to attach. The two ground pins on each side are joined.
notes: Side 2 can instead run from a 5 V VBUS2, wired the same way as side 1.
The 24 Ω resistors are needed only at full speed.
Lead length from both ends of each bypass capacitor to the supply pin totals 10 mm or less.

operation.text: Each side watches its inputs. A transition out of the idle J state on one side sets that side as the source; the far side turns on its output buffers and stops edge detection on its own inputs, while the source side keeps its outputs off, so data cannot loop back through the barrier. Transfer continues until an end-of-packet or a long enough idle, after which both sides release their buffers and wait for the next activity. Direction is decided packet by packet.

Only three line states are sent across: J, K and SE0. The output side rebuilds the signal with a fixed delay from the differential input. Invalid SE0 and SE1 transients are not passed, and internal logic hides any glitch caused by the single-ended and differential receivers switching at different levels.
There is no suspend mode. With the bus idle, supply current stays below the 2.5 mA USB suspend limit.

An upstream-facing port runs at one speed, so the J/K logic levels, slew rate and timing are fixed by strapping SPU on side 1 and SPD on side 2. Both must be set the same and match the peripheral's speed: high for 12 Mbps full speed, low for 1.5 Mbps low speed.

The upstream pull-up and the downstream pull-downs are inside the part. Enumeration starts when the pull-up raises UD+ or UD- at the cable end; PIN on side 2 switches that pull-up, so it can be tied to VDD2, to the peripheral's own pull-up, or to a control line to choose when the device attaches. Beyond this delayed attach, USB traffic passes unchanged and the peripheral design needs no changes.
PDEN is read on leaving reset. Tied to VDD1 the downstream pull-downs are connected as normal; held at GND1 at that moment they are disconnected, which allows the buffer impedance to be measured.

The added propagation delay is similar to that of a hub and cable, so an isolated peripheral counts as having a built-in hub when totting up hub tiers. An ADuM4160 on the upstream port of a hub chip makes an isolated hub, which complies when it is budgeted as two hub delays; the hub chip then lets the isolator run at full speed while still serving low speed devices.

Both sides can drive USB cables, so the part can isolate a downstream (host) port or a cable. A compliant downstream port must sense a device's speed from its pull-up and adapt; with speed strapped, such a port works at one speed only. That suits embedded hosts but is not a fully compliant general-purpose port, and an isolated cable likewise runs only at its preset speed.

Each side has a VBUSx and a VDDx pin and an internal LDO. With 5 V on VBUSx the LDO makes 3.3 V to run the xD+ and xD- drivers, and VDDx gives access to that rail for bypassing and for biasing pull-ups. With only 3.3 V available, feed it to both VBUSx and VDDx; the regulator is then disabled and the side runs straight from the 3.3 V supply.

If side 1 loses VDD1, the downstream drivers go high impedance within 32 bit times, and side 2 starts up in high impedance. If side 2 loses VDD2, side 1 removes its pull-up and disables its UD+ and UD- drivers inside 32 bit times. PIN low also leaves side 1 looking disconnected.

Each input edge sends a pulse of about 1 ns across the transformer to a bistable decoder. When the input has not changed for roughly 12 USB bit times, refresh pulses carrying the present state are sent. If the decoder sees no pulses for roughly 36 bit times it takes the input side as unpowered or faulty, and a watchdog forces the output to its default state.

Transformer output pulses exceed 1.0 V and the decoder threshold is about 0.5 V, leaving 0.5 V of margin; the 3 V operating condition is the most sensitive. At 1 MHz a 0.2 kgauss field induces 0.25 V, about half the threshold, and causes no false transition; if it coincides with a pulse of the worst polarity the pulse drops from more than 1.0 V to 0.75 V, still above threshold. At 1 MHz it would take 0.5 kA flowing 5 mm from the part to disturb it. Under strong high-frequency fields, loops in PCB traces can themselves induce enough voltage to upset following circuits.

The logic interfaces need no external circuits. At full speed each D+ and D- line on both sides takes a 24 Ω ±1% series resistor; low speed needs none. Bypass every supply pin with 0.1 µF low-ESR capacitors, keeping the total lead length between the capacitor ends and the supply pin to 10 mm or less. Also consider bypassing between pins 2 and 8 and between pins 9 and 15, unless each side's ground pair is joined close to the package.

Where common-mode transients are large, keep board coupling across the barrier small, and lay out so that whatever coupling remains reaches all pins of one side equally; uneven coupling can push pin-to-pin voltages past the absolute maximum and cause latch-up or permanent damage.

Insulation wears out under voltage stress at a rate set by the waveform across the barrier. Bipolar ac is the hardest case and sets the 565 V peak working voltage for a 50-year life. Unipolar ac (varying between 0 V and a limit of either sign without crossing 0 V) and dc stress the insulation much less, so the higher approved working voltages hold for 50 years with those waveforms. A waveform that is neither should be treated as bipolar ac and kept to the 50-year bipolar value. The approved working voltage may exceed the 50-year value, and running at it can shorten insulation life.
